disposition_reason: Table 2 prints mean ± SD (mg/L) of As, Cd, Co, Cu, Mn, Pb and Zn for 18 packaged soft-drink and malt-drink products bought in Ile-Ife, Nigeria.

study.design: Market survey of 18 sets of soft drinks and malt drinks in three packaging types (glass bottle, plastic bottle, can); triplicate analysis
study.market: wholesale stores and outlets in Ile-Ife, Nigeria
study.method: Flame AAS (PG 990) after HNO3/HClO4 hotplate digestion of 20 mL drink
study.qa: Blank determination; spike recoveries As 96.9, Cd 92.3, Co 95.4, Cu 96.5, Mn 87.6, Pb 95.9, Zn 98.2%; calibration r2 0.9878-0.9991 (Table 1); no CRM

findings.group: retail soft drink product 1, glass bottle
findings.notes: Per-litre value not converted to µg/kg. Paper code CCB; product identities are not given in the text (codes ending B = glass bottle and P = plastic bottle per Section 3.2; C taken as can by elimination). Products 7-9 have pH 3.9-4.3 and are probably the malt products named in the title, but the paper does not say. Flame-AAS values far above usual soft-drink levels; analytical plausibility uncertain. SD 0.01 mg/L (unconverted).
